```{r libraries, echo=FALSE}
# Data handling and utilities
library(tidyverse)   # also attaches dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, forcats, purrr, lubridate
library(here)
library(labelled)    # variable labels

# Tables
library(gtsummary)
library(gt)

# Models, imputation and marginal means
library(cvcrand)     # cptest(): permutation test for cluster-randomized trials
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)    # p-values for lmer (attached after lme4 so lmer() is the lmerTest version)
library(mice)
library(mitools)     # MIcombine(): Rubin's rules for marginal means
library(mitml)       # pooled likelihood-ratio (D3) global tests
library(pan)         # 2l.pan multilevel imputation method
library(broom.mixed) # tidiers used by tbl_regression() for mixed models
library(emmeans)

# Survival plots
library(ggsurvfit)

# Loaded in the original report but not used anywhere in this document (candidates to remove):
# library(haven); library(kableExtra); library(ggpubr); library(ggmosaic); library(flextable)
```

```{r config, echo=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# ANALYSIS SETTINGS -- edit this chunk to change constants and re-run analyses
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Files -------------------------------------------------------------------
data_file              <- here::here("data", "EMPRO_data_20261008.RData")
randscheme_path        <- "//duhsnas-pri.dhe.duke.edu/home/leh36/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/randscheme_final.csv"   # site-level covariates
constrained_space_path <- "//duhsnas-pri.dhe.duke.edu/home/leh36/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/empro_constrained.csv"  # constrained randomization space (cptest)

# ---- Analysis population and study constants ---------------------------------
max_enrollment_month <- 45                     # exclude participants enrolled after this study month
bug_fix_date         <- as.Date("2024-07-19")  # consent after this date = enrolled after the technical bug was fixed
bug_visits           <- paste("Month", 1:6)    # visits in which bug exposure is counted
eortc_months         <- c(6, 12)               # EORTC time points to transform and analyze

# Site order must match the order used when randomizing (and the constrained space file)
site_order <- c("Queensland University of Technology",
                "Eastern Health",
                "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
                "Macquarie University Hospital",
                "Cross Cancer Institute",
                "Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre",
                "The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust",
                "Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust",
                "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
                "University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust",
                "Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center",
                "Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center",
                "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
                "University of Virginia")

# ---- Outcome transformation --------------------------------------------------
eortc_max       <- 100                              # maximum possible EORTC composite score
eortc_trans     <- function(x) sqrt(eortc_max - x)  # reflected square root (corrects left skew)
inv_eortc_trans <- function(x) eortc_max - x^2      # back-transform to the original 0-100 scale
trans           <- paste0("√(", eortc_max, "-x)")   # label used in text and plot titles

# ---- Model specification -----------------------------------------------------
exposure_var <- "arm_c"                                                        # treatment arm
subject_covs <- c("age_baseline", "ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per")   # subject-level covariates
site_covs    <- c("site_country", "site_timetodx", "site_crpc")                # site-level covariates from the randomization scheme
adj_terms    <- c(subject_covs, site_covs)                                     # all adjustment terms
random_term  <- "(1 | sitenew)"                                                # random intercept for site

categorical_covs <- c("ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per", "site_country")  # factors (tells cptest which z columns are categorical)
global_test_vars <- c("ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "site_country")              # multi-level factors shown with a global p-value

# Row labels used in every regression table (only labels for variables in the model are used)
covariate_labels <- list(
  arm_c         = "Treatment Arm",
  full_dose     = "Bug impact",
  age_baseline  = "Age",
  ecog3         = "ECOG Performance Status",
  race_gp       = "Race",
  educ_gp       = "Education Level",
  crpc_per      = "Disease State",
  site_country  = "Country",
  site_timetodx = "Time from Diagnosis to Enrollment (Site-Level)",
  site_crpc     = "CRPC (Site-Level)")

# ---- Multiple imputation settings --------------------------------------------
n_imp    <- 100   # number of imputed data sets
n_iter   <- 1     # mice iterations (only the outcome is imputed)
imp_seed <- 123   # seed for mice

# ---- MNAR shift constants ----------------------------------------------------
# Shifts are in raw EORTC points (negative = worse QoL than predicted under MAR) and are
# named by the level of `shift_var`. Other options considered: mild = 0 / -5 / -10 and
# upper = 0 / -10 / -20 for ECOG 0 / 1 / 2-4 (5-10 pts = small, 10-20 pts = moderate difference).
shift_var     <- "ecog3"
delta_large   <- c(`0` = 0, `1` = -7,   `2-4` = -12, Unknown = 0)  # large shifts applied to imputed scores
delta_small   <- c(`0` = 0, `1` = -3.5, `2-4` = -6,   Unknown = 0)  # more conservative shifts
p_shift_ecog  <- c(`0` = 0, `1` = 0.5, `2-4` = 0.5, Unknown = 0.5)  # 'variable' scenario: probability a participant is shifted
sd_shift_ecog <- c(`0` = 2, `1` = 3,   `2-4` = 4,   Unknown = 3)    # optional: SD of random noise around delta (set sd_shift in a scenario)

# ---- Imputation scenarios ----------------------------------------------------
# Each scenario is passed to run_mi_scenario(). To run a new analysis, edit a scenario or add one.
#   delta        named vector of shifts; NULL = plain MAR imputation (no post-processing)
#   p_shift      named vector of probabilities that a participant is shifted; NULL = everyone shifted ("fixed")
#   sd_shift     named vector of noise SDs added around delta; NULL = no noise (use p_shift OR sd_shift, not both)
#   score_deaths TRUE = participants who died by the time point get the worst EORTC score instead of being imputed
#   emm_method   how pooled marginal means are computed: "rubin" (per-imputation emmeans + Rubin's rules)
#                or "mira" (emmeans applied directly to the pooled mira object)
# make_scenario() stores the constants it is given, so each scenario keeps its own shifts.
# (Changing delta_large / delta_small AFTER this point has no effect on scenarios already created.)
make_scenario <- function(label, caption, delta = NULL, p_shift = NULL, sd_shift = NULL,
                          score_deaths = !is.null(delta), emm_method = "rubin") {
  list(label = label, caption = caption, delta = delta, p_shift = p_shift, sd_shift = sd_shift,
       score_deaths = score_deaths, emm_method = emm_method)
}

mi_scenarios <- list(
  mar = make_scenario(
    label        = "MAR imputation",
    caption      = "**Analysis of primary outcome with missing EORTC imputed under MAR assumptions**",
    score_deaths = FALSE,
    emm_method   = "mira"),
  fixed_large = make_scenario(
    label   = "MNAR imputation - large fixed shift",
    caption = "**Analysis of primary outcome with missing EORTC imputed under MNAR assumptions (large ECOG-dependent downward shift; deaths scored 0)**",
    delta   = delta_large),
  fixed_small = make_scenario(
    label   = "MNAR imputation - small fixed shift",
    caption = "**Analysis of primary outcome with missing EORTC imputed under MNAR assumptions (small ECOG-dependent downward shift; deaths scored 0)**",
    delta   = delta_small),
  variable_large = make_scenario(
    label   = "MNAR imputation - large variable shift",
    caption = "**Analysis of primary outcome with missing EORTC imputed under MNAR assumptions (large ECOG-dependent downward shift applied with probability p; deaths scored 0)**",
    delta   = delta_large, p_shift = p_shift_ecog),
  variable_small = make_scenario(
    label   = "MNAR imputation - small variable shift",
    caption = "**Analysis of primary outcome with missing EORTC imputed under MNAR assumptions (small ECOG-dependent downward shift applied with probability p; deaths scored 0)**",
    delta   = delta_small, p_shift = p_shift_ecog)
)
```

```{r functions-modeling, echo=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# FUNCTIONS (modeling and imputation)
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Outcome / formula helpers -----------------------------------------------

# Names of the variables that belong to one EORTC time point (month = 6, 12, ...)
outcome_spec <- function(month) {
  list(month = month,
       raw   = paste0("eortc_", month),          # raw 0-100 score
       norm  = paste0("eortc_", month, "norm"),  # transformed score (the modeled outcome)
       dead  = paste0("dead", month))            # death indicator by this time point
}

# outcome ~ term1 + term2 + ... + (1 | sitenew)
build_formula <- function(outcome, terms, random = random_term) {
  reformulate(c(terms, random), response = outcome)
}

# Keep only the labels for variables that are in the model (tbl_regression errors on extras)
labels_for <- function(model, labels = covariate_labels) {
  labels[names(labels) %in% all.vars(formula(model))]
}

# ---- Text helpers (inline narrative always matches the shifts that were actually run) ----------
ecog_names <- c(`0` = "ECOG 0", `1` = "ECOG 1", `2-4` = "ECOG 2–4", Unknown = "participants missing ECOG")

# "no shift for ECOG 0, down by approximately 7 points for ECOG 1, ..., and ..."
describe_shifts <- function(delta) {
  parts <- vapply(names(delta), function(l)
    if (delta[[l]] == 0) paste("no shift for", ecog_names[[l]])
    else paste0("down by approximately ", abs(delta[[l]]), " points for ", ecog_names[[l]]), character(1))
  paste0(paste(parts[-length(parts)], collapse = ", "), ", and ", parts[length(parts)])
}

# "−7 for ECOG 1, −12 for ECOG 2–4, 0 for unknown ECOG"
shift_list <- function(delta) {
  d <- delta[names(delta) != "0"]
  lab <- c(`1` = "ECOG 1", `2-4` = "ECOG 2–4", Unknown = "unknown ECOG")[names(d)]
  paste0(ifelse(d == 0, "0", paste0("−", abs(d))), " for ", lab, collapse = ", ")
}

# probabilities as text, e.g. "0.5" or "0.3–0.6"
p_text <- function(p) paste(unique(p[p > 0]), collapse = "–")

# ---- Complete case analysis --------------------------------------------------

# Linear mixed model fit to complete cases (REML), via lmerTest for p-values/df
fit_cc_model <- function(data, outcome, exposure = exposure_var,
                         terms = adj_terms, random = random_term) {
  f <- build_formula(outcome, c(exposure, terms), random)
  do.call(lmerTest::lmer, list(formula = f, data = data, REML = TRUE))
}

# Residual diagnostics: residuals vs fitted, histogram, normal Q-Q
plot_lmm_diagnostics <- function(fit) {
  res <- resid(fit)
  fv  <- fitted(fit)
  plot(fv, res, xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals")
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  hist(res, breaks = 30, main = "Residuals", xlab = "Residual value")
  qqnorm(res)
  qqline(res)
}

# Permutation test (cvcrand::cptest) for the intervention effect.
# `covs` are the covariates to adjust for; categorical ones are detected from `categorical_covs`.
run_cptest <- function(data, outcome, covs, categorical = categorical_covs,
                       cspace = constrained_space_path) {
  cptest(outcome       = data[[outcome]],
         clustername   = data$sitenew,
         z             = data.frame(data[, covs]),
         cspacedatname = cspace,
         outcometype   = "continuous",
         categorical   = intersect(categorical, covs))
}

# ---- Multiple imputation -----------------------------------------------------

# Build the data set passed to mice (subject, outcome, exposure, covariates, site as integer cluster id).
# If dead_var is given, participants who died with a missing outcome get the worst EORTC score
# (eortc_trans(0)) and are flagged in `ignore` so mice does not use them to fit the imputation model.
prep_impute_data <- function(data, outcome, dead_var = NULL, exposure = exposure_var) {
  ignore <- NULL
  if (!is.null(dead_var)) {
    dead <- !is.na(data[[dead_var]]) & data[[dead_var]] == 1
    data[[outcome]] <- ifelse(dead & is.na(data[[outcome]]), eortc_trans(0), data[[outcome]])
    ignore <- dead
  }
  imp_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("subject", outcome, exposure, subject_covs, "sitenew", site_covs))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sitenew = as.integer(factor(sitenew)))

  # Only the outcome may have missing values
  other_na <- colSums(is.na(imp_data[setdiff(names(imp_data), outcome)]))
  if (any(other_na > 0))
    stop("Missing values in imputation predictors: ",
         paste(names(other_na)[other_na > 0], collapse = ", "))

  list(data = imp_data, ignore = ignore)
}

# Text of the mice post-processing code that shifts imputed values (evaluated inside mice).
# Imputations are made on the transformed scale, so each value is back-transformed to raw EORTC
# points, shifted by delta (bounded to 0-eortc_max), and transformed again.
#   delta only          -> every imputed value shifted by delta ("fixed")
#   delta + p_shift     -> shifted with probability p_shift, otherwise left as MAR
#   delta + sd_shift    -> shifted by delta plus Normal(0, sd_shift) noise
make_post_code <- function(delta, p_shift = NULL, sd_shift = NULL,
                           shift_var = "ecog3", max_score = eortc_max) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(delta), !is.null(names(delta)))
  if (!is.null(p_shift) && !is.null(sd_shift)) stop("Use either p_shift or sd_shift, not both")
  as_code <- function(x) paste(deparse(x), collapse = "")   # named vector -> R code

  shift_lines <-
    if (!is.null(p_shift)) {
      c("shifted <- rbinom(length(lev), size = 1, prob = unname(p_shift[lev]))",
        "d <- unname(delta[lev]) * shifted")
    } else if (!is.null(sd_shift)) {
      c("d <- unname(delta[lev]) + rnorm(length(lev), mean = 0, sd = unname(sd_shift[lev]))")
    } else {
      "d <- unname(delta[lev])"
    }

  paste(c(
    paste("delta <-", as_code(delta)),
    if (!is.null(p_shift))  paste("p_shift <-", as_code(p_shift)),
    if (!is.null(sd_shift)) paste("sd_shift <-", as_code(sd_shift)),
    # rows of the original data being imputed in this variable
    "rows <- match(rownames(imp[[j]]), rownames(data))",
    sprintf("lev  <- as.character(data[[%s]][rows])", deparse(shift_var)),
    "if (anyNA(rows) || any(!lev %in% names(delta))) stop('Unmatched row or shift-variable level in post function')",
    shift_lines,
    sprintf("z <- pmin(pmax(imp[[j]][, i], 0), %s)", format(sqrt(max_score))),  # keep on the valid transformed scale
    sprintf("x <- %s - z^2", format(max_score)),                                  # back-transform to raw points
    sprintf("x_shifted <- pmin(pmax(x + d, 0), %s)", format(max_score)),          # apply shift, keep within 0-max
    sprintf("imp[[j]][, i] <- sqrt(%s - x_shifted)", format(max_score))           # transform again
  ), collapse = "\n")
}

# mice's 2l.pan returns one imputed value for EVERY row with ry == FALSE. When `ignore` is used (here:
# deaths), the ignored rows have ry == FALSE too, so the returned vector is longer than the number of
# rows being imputed and mice assigns the values to the wrong participants (it only warns "number of
# items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length"). This wrapper keeps only the values for
# the rows that are actually imputed (wy). Without `ignore` it gives identical results to 2l.pan.
mice.impute.2l.pan_aligned <- function(y, ry, x, wy, type, ...) {
  res <- mice::mice.impute.2l.pan(y = y, ry = ry, x = x, type = type, ...)
  res[wy[!ry]]
}
assign("mice.impute.2l.pan_aligned", mice.impute.2l.pan_aligned, envir = globalenv())

# Impute the outcome only, using the two-level normal model (2l.pan) with site as the cluster.
# aligned = FALSE reproduces plain "2l.pan" (only relevant when `ignore` is supplied; see above).
impute_outcome <- function(imp_data, outcome, post_code = NULL, ignore = NULL, aligned = TRUE,
                           m = n_imp, maxit = n_iter, seed = imp_seed) {
  meth <- make.method(imp_data)
  meth[] <- ""                       # do not impute anything else
  meth[outcome] <- if (aligned) "2l.pan_aligned" else "2l.pan"

  pred <- make.predictorMatrix(imp_data)
  pred[outcome, ] <- 1                                # all variables predict the outcome...
  pred[outcome, c("subject", outcome)] <- 0           # ...except the ID and the outcome itself
  pred[outcome, "sitenew"] <- -2                      # -2 = cluster variable for multilevel imputation

  post <- make.post(imp_data)
  if (!is.null(post_code)) post[outcome] <- post_code

  mice(imp_data, m = m, maxit = maxit, seed = seed, method = meth,
       predictorMatrix = pred, post = post, ignore = ignore, printFlag = FALSE)
}

# Check that the shift constants cover every level that will actually be imputed
check_shift_inputs <- function(imp_data, outcome, scenario, shift_var) {
  stopifnot(shift_var %in% names(imp_data))
  lev_missing <- unique(as.character(imp_data[[shift_var]][is.na(imp_data[[outcome]])]))
  for (nm in c("delta", "p_shift", "sd_shift")) {
    v <- scenario[[nm]]
    if (!is.null(v) && length(setdiff(lev_missing, names(v))))
      stop(nm, " has no value for: ", paste(setdiff(lev_missing, names(v)), collapse = ", "))
  }
}

# Run one imputation scenario end to end: impute -> fit lmer in each imputation -> global p-values.
# `spec` comes from outcome_spec(); `scenario` is one element of mi_scenarios.
run_mi_scenario <- function(data, spec, scenario, exposure = exposure_var, shift_by = shift_var) {
  prep <- prep_impute_data(data, spec$norm,
                           dead_var = if (isTRUE(scenario$score_deaths)) spec$dead,
                           exposure = exposure)
  post_code <- NULL
  if (!is.null(scenario$delta)) {
    check_shift_inputs(prep$data, spec$norm, scenario, shift_by)
    post_code <- make_post_code(scenario$delta, scenario$p_shift, scenario$sd_shift, shift_by)
  }
  imp <- impute_outcome(prep$data, spec$norm, post_code = post_code, ignore = prep$ignore)
  list(imp      = imp,
       fit      = fit_mi_models(imp, spec$norm, exposure),
       global_p = pooled_global_pvals(imp, spec$norm, exposure),
       spec     = spec,
       exposure = exposure,
       scenario = scenario)
}

# Fit the adjusted mixed model (ML) in every imputed data set; returns a mira object
fit_mi_models <- function(imp, outcome, exposure = exposure_var,
                          terms = adj_terms, random = random_term) {
  fml <- deparse1(build_formula(outcome, c(exposure, terms), random))
  with(imp, lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(fml), REML = FALSE))
}

# Global (omnibus) p-value for each variable in global_vars: pooled likelihood-ratio test (D3,
# Meng & Rubin 1992) comparing the full model with a model that omits the variable.
pooled_global_pvals <- function(imp, outcome, exposure = exposure_var, terms = adj_terms,
                                global_vars = global_test_vars, random = random_term) {
  imp_list  <- mitml::mids2mitml.list(imp)          # plain list of completed data sets
  all_terms <- c(exposure, terms)

  fit_models <- function(trm) {
    f    <- build_formula(outcome, trm, random)
    fits <- lapply(imp_list, function(d)
      do.call(lmerTest::lmer, list(formula = f, data = d, REML = FALSE)))
    class(fits) <- c("mitml.result", "list")
    fits
  }

  full <- fit_models(all_terms)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(global_vars, function(v) {
    reduced <- fit_models(setdiff(all_terms, v))
    tt      <- mitml::testModels(full, reduced, method = "D3")
    tibble::tibble(variable = v, row_type = "label", p.value = tt$test[, "P(>F)"])
  }))
}

# ---- Estimated marginal means ------------------------------------------------

# Pooled estimated marginal means (transformed scale) across imputations
#   "rubin": emmeans in each imputation, combined with Rubin's rules (mitools::MIcombine)
#   "mira" : emmeans applied directly to the pooled mira object
pooled_emm <- function(fit_mira, spec = exposure_var, method = c("rubin", "mira"), alpha = 0.05) {
  method <- match.arg(method)
  specs  <- reformulate(spec)
  if (method == "mira") return(as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(fit_mira, specs)))

  emm_list <- lapply(fit_mira$analyses, emmeans::emmeans, specs = specs, lmer.df = "asymptotic")
  mi    <- mitools::MIcombine(lapply(emm_list, function(x) summary(x)$emmean),         # estimates
                              lapply(emm_list, function(x) as.matrix(vcov(x))))         # variances
  est   <- as.numeric(mi$coefficients)
  se    <- sqrt(diag(mi$variance))
  tcrit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df = mi$df)

  out <- data.frame(summary(emm_list[[1]])[[spec]], est, se, est - tcrit * se, est + tcrit * se)
  names(out) <- c(spec, "emmean", "SE", "lower.CL", "upper.CL")
  out
}

# Back-transform marginal means and CIs to the raw EORTC scale (rounded to 1 decimal).
# The transformation is decreasing, so the CI limits swap; pmin/pmax puts them back in order.
backtransform_emm <- function(emm_df, group_var) {
  emm_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(mean_orig  = inv_eortc_trans(emmean),
                  a          = inv_eortc_trans(lower.CL),
                  b          = inv_eortc_trans(upper.CL),
                  lower_orig = pmin(a, b),
                  upper_orig = pmax(a, b)) %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(group_var), mean_orig, lower_orig, upper_orig) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mean_orig, lower_orig, upper_orig), ~ round(.x, 1)))
}
```

```{r functions-plots, echo=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# FUNCTIONS (plots)
# ==============================================================================

# Common plot theme (bold, centered titles; larger axis text). Optional facet-label size and bottom legend.
theme_empro <- function(strip_size = NULL, legend_bottom = FALSE) {
  th <- theme_bw() +
    theme(plot.title   = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
          axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16),
          axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 14),
          axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.70, face = "bold", size = 18),
          axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 14))
  if (!is.null(strip_size)) th <- th + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = strip_size))
  if (legend_bottom)        th <- th + theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
                                             legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
                                             legend.position = "bottom")
  th
}

# Histogram of one EORTC variable (optionally one panel per arm)
plot_eortc_hist <- function(data, var, title, xlab, binwidth = NULL, facet_arm = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[var]])) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = "#a6dba0", color = "black") +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = "Frequency")
  if (facet_arm) p <- p + facet_wrap(~ arm_c)
  p + theme_empro(strip_size = if (facet_arm) 12)
}

# The three histograms shown for each time point: raw score, transformed score, transformed score by arm
eortc_hist_plots <- function(data, month) {
  o <- outcome_spec(month)
  list(
    raw         = plot_eortc_hist(data, o$raw,
                                  paste0("EORTC at ", month, " Months"), "EORTC Score", binwidth = 5),
    transformed = plot_eortc_hist(data, o$norm,
                                  paste0("EORTC at ", month, " months ", trans), paste0("EORTC Score ", trans)),
    by_arm      = plot_eortc_hist(data, o$norm,
                                  paste0("EORTC Score ", trans), paste0("EORTC Score ", trans),
                                  binwidth = 0.6, facet_arm = TRUE))
}

# Compare the distribution of observed (complete case) outcomes with the values *imputed* under each
# scenario. `results` is a list of run_mi_scenario() results. Values are on the transformed scale.
compare_eortc_distributions <- function(data, outcome, results) {
  keep <- c("subject", "ecog3", outcome, "source")   # columns needed for plotting

  observed <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(source = "Complete case") %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(keep))

  # keep only the imputed values (rows whose outcome was missing in the imputation data set)
  imputed <- lapply(results, function(r) {
    mice::complete(r$imp, action = "long") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(source = r$scenario$label,
                    was_missing = is.na(r$imp$data[[outcome]][match(subject, r$imp$data$subject)])) %>%
      dplyr::filter(was_missing) %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(keep))
  })

  all_values <- dplyr::bind_rows(c(list(observed), unname(imputed)))

  overall <- ggplot(all_values, aes(x = .data[[outcome]], fill = source)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
    labs(title = "Distribution of EORTC scores",
         subtitle = "Complete cases vs MAR and ECOG-adjusted imputations",
         x = "EORTC score", y = "Density") +
    theme_empro()

  by_ecog <- ggplot(all_values, aes(x = .data[[outcome]], fill = source)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~ ecog3) +
    labs(title = "EORTC distributions by ECOG score",
         subtitle = "Observed vs MAR vs MNAR imputations",
         x = "EORTC score (transformed scale)", y = "Density") +
    theme_empro() +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

  list(overall = overall, by_ecog = by_ecog)
}
```

```{r functions-tables, echo=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# FUNCTIONS (tables)
# ==============================================================================

# Baseline characteristics of one arm, by site
tbl_baseline_by_site <- function(data, arm_value) {
  data %>%
    dplyr::filter(arm == arm_value) %>%
    dplyr::select(site, age_baseline, race_gp, year_emp_enrollment,
                  enrollment_month1, crpc_per, educ_gp, ecog2) %>%
    tbl_summary(by = site,
                missing = "ifany",
                missing_text = "N missing",
                type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
                statistic = all_continuous() ~ c("{median} ({p25}, {p75})",
                                                 "{min}, {max}")) %>%
    bold_labels() %>%
    modify_header(label = "") %>%
    modify_caption(paste0("**Baseline participant characteristics in the ", arm_value, " arm by site**"))
}

# Regression table for a complete case model: term p-values for continuous/binary variables,
# global (ANOVA) p-values for the multi-level factors in `global_vars`
tbl_cc_regression <- function(fit, caption, labels = covariate_labels, global_vars = global_test_vars) {
  lab <- labels_for(fit, labels)

  # table with term-level p-values
  main_tab <- tbl_regression(fit, label = lab) %>%
    bold_labels()

  # table with global p-values only
  global_p_tab <- tbl_regression(fit, label = lab) %>%
    add_global_p() %>%
    bold_labels() %>%
    modify_column_hide(estimate) %>%
    modify_column_hide(conf.low)

  tbl_merge(list(main_tab, global_p_tab)) %>%
    modify_spanning_header(everything() ~ NA_character_) %>%
    modify_header(p.value_1 ~ "**P-value**",
                  p.value_2 ~ "**Global p-value**") %>%
    # keep the term p-value for variables tested one-df, and the global p-value for the factors
    modify_table_body(
      ~ .x %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          p.value_1 = dplyr::if_else(variable %in% global_vars, NA_real_, p.value_1),
          p.value_2 = dplyr::if_else(variable %in% global_vars, p.value_2, NA_real_))) %>%
    modify_footnote(p.value_2 ~ "Global p-values obtained from ANOVA") %>%
    modify_caption(caption)
}

# Regression table for a pooled (multiply imputed) model from run_mi_scenario()
tbl_mi_regression <- function(res, caption = res$scenario$caption,
                              labels = covariate_labels, global_vars = global_test_vars) {
  tbl_regression(res$fit, label = labels_for(res$fit$analyses[[1]], labels)) %>%
    # term p-values kept for non-global variables; pooled global p-values joined in for the factors
    modify_table_body(
      ~ .x %>%
        dplyr::rename(original.p = p.value) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(original.p = scales::pvalue(original.p)) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(res$global_p, by = c("variable", "row_type")) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          original.p = dplyr::if_else(variable %in% global_vars, NA_character_, original.p),
          p.value    = dplyr::if_else(variable %in% global_vars, p.value, NA_real_))) %>%
    modify_column_unhide(columns = c(original.p, p.value)) %>%
    modify_header(original.p ~ "**P-value**",
                  p.value ~ "**Global p-value**") %>%
    bold_labels() %>%
    modify_footnote(
      all_stat_cols() ~ "Estimates pooled across multiple imputations using Rubin\u2019s rules.") %>%
    modify_footnote(
      p.value ~ "Global p-values are calculated from a pooled likelihood-ratio test (D3; Meng & Rubin, 1992) comparing the full mixed model with a model omitting that variable, with other covariates and a random site intercept retained.") %>%
    modify_caption(caption)
}

# gt table of back-transformed marginal means
gt_emm_table <- function(emm_df, group_var = exposure_var, group_label = "Treatment Arm",
                         title = "Adjusted estimate (back-transformed) by treatment arm",
                         subtitle = NULL, note = NULL) {
  tab <- gt(emm_df) %>%
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) %>%
    cols_label(.list = c(setNames(list(group_label), group_var),
                         list(mean_orig  = "Adjusted Mean",
                              lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
                              upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI")))
  if (!is.null(note)) tab <- tab %>% tab_source_note(source_note = note)
  tab
}

# Back-transformed marginal means for a complete case model
emm_table_cc <- function(fit, exposure = exposure_var, ...) {
  emm <- as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(fit, reformulate(exposure)))
  gt_emm_table(backtransform_emm(emm, exposure), exposure, ...)
}

# Back-transformed pooled marginal means for a run_mi_scenario() result
emm_table_mi <- function(res, method = res$scenario$emm_method, ...) {
  emm <- pooled_emm(res$fit, res$exposure, method = method)
  gt_emm_table(backtransform_emm(emm, res$exposure), res$exposure, ...)
}

# Back-transformed marginal means from several analyses stacked in one data frame (one block per method).
# `cc_fit` is a complete case lmer fit; `mi_results` is a list of run_mi_scenario() results.
# Each analysis is its own block even if two scenarios share the same label.
# `method_labels` (optional) sets the group headers:
#   - an unnamed vector, one label per analysis in table order (complete case first), or
#   - a named vector that renames every block whose default label matches, e.g. c("MAR imputation" = "MAR")
emm_combined_df <- function(cc_fit, mi_results, exposure = exposure_var, method_labels = NULL) {
  cc <- as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(cc_fit, reformulate(exposure))) %>%
    backtransform_emm(exposure) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(method = "Complete case")

  mi <- lapply(mi_results, function(r) {
    pooled_emm(r$fit, r$exposure, method = r$scenario$emm_method) %>%
      backtransform_emm(r$exposure) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(method = r$scenario$label)
  })

  blocks  <- c(list(cc), unname(mi))
  labels  <- vapply(blocks, function(x) x$method[1], character(1))   # default header of each block

  if (!is.null(method_labels)) {
    if (is.null(names(method_labels))) {
      if (length(method_labels) != length(blocks))
        stop("method_labels has ", length(method_labels), " labels but the table has ", length(blocks),
             " analyses (complete case + ", length(mi), " imputation results)")
      labels <- unname(method_labels)
    } else {
      unknown <- setdiff(names(method_labels), labels)
      if (length(unknown))
        stop("method_labels names not found: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "),
             ". Default labels are: ", paste(unique(labels), collapse = ", "))
      hit <- labels %in% names(method_labels)
      labels[hit] <- unname(method_labels[labels[hit]])
    }
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(labels))
    stop("Two analyses have the same header (", paste(unique(labels[duplicated(labels)]), collapse = ", "),
         "). Give each a distinct label with method_labels, in table order.")

  blocks <- Map(function(x, l) dplyr::mutate(x, method = l), blocks, labels)
  dplyr::bind_rows(blocks) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(method = factor(method, levels = labels),
                  dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(exposure), as.character)) %>%
    dplyr::select(method, dplyr::everything())
}

# One gt table of back-transformed marginal means for every analysis, grouped by method
emm_table_combined <- function(cc_fit, mi_results, exposure = exposure_var, method_labels = NULL,
                               group_label = "Treatment Arm",
                               title = "Adjusted estimates (back-transformed) by treatment arm and analysis method",
                               subtitle = NULL, note = NULL) {
  tab <- emm_combined_df(cc_fit, mi_results, exposure, method_labels) %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "method") %>%
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) %>%
    cols_label(.list = c(setNames(list(group_label), exposure),
                         list(mean_orig  = "Adjusted Mean",
                              lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
                              upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI")))
  if (!is.null(note)) tab <- tab %>% tab_source_note(source_note = note)
  tab
}

```

```{r readdata, echo = F, include = F}
# ==============================================================================
# DATA PREPARATION
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
load(data_file)   # objects used below: empro_data, triggers_long, not_matched

# enrollment month as a factor
empro_data$enrollment_month1 = factor(empro_data$enrollment_month)

# yes/no CRPC (anything other than mHSPC)
empro_data$crpc_per = empro_data$cohort_empro != "mHSPC"

# flag for participants who were not matched
empro_data$not_matched = ifelse(empro_data$subject %in% not_matched, 1, 0)

# relabel new variables
var_label(empro_data) <- list(
  enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry")

# site-level data from the randomization scheme
site_data <- read.csv(randscheme_path) %>% 
  rename(site_country = Country,
         site_timetodx = timetodx,
         site_crpc = CRPC)

# ---- Technical bug exposure --------------------------------------------------
# Proportion of intervention questionnaires in the first 6 months completed while the bug was present
bug_outcome <- triggers_long %>% 
  filter(visit %in% bug_visits) %>% 
  mutate(bug = ifelse(after_bug=="Bug present", 1, 0)) %>% 
  group_by(subject) %>% 
  summarize(n_bug = sum(bug),
            n_total = n()) %>% 
  select(subject, n_bug, n_total) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(p_bug = n_bug/n_total,
         bug_group = case_when(
           p_bug==0 ~ 1,
           p_bug>0 & p_bug<1 ~ 2,
           p_bug==1 ~ 3))

# ---- Analysis data set (apply exclusions) ------------------------------------
analysis_data <- empro_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(empro_cnstdate) & enrollment_month<=max_enrollment_month & !is.na(cohort_empro)) %>%
  mutate(enrollment_month1 = fct_drop(enrollment_month1)) %>%
  # harmonize site names to match the randomization scheme (case_when uses the original `site` value)
  mutate(sitenew = case_when(
    site=="Cross Cancer Institute (Alberta Health Services)" ~ "Cross Cancer Institute",
    site=="Guys St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust" ~ "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
    #site=="Royal Brisbane & Women’s Hospital" ~ "Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital",
    site=="St. Vincent’s Hospital Sydney" ~ "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
    site=="University of Virgina (UVA)" ~ "University of Virginia", 
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital" ~ "Queensland University of Technology",
    site=="NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital" ~ "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
    TRUE ~ site),
    ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown"),    # ECOG with an explicit "Unknown" category
    crpc_per = factor(crpc_per, levels=c("FALSE", "TRUE"), labels = c("mHSPC", "CRPC"))) %>% 
  left_join(site_data, by = c("sitenew"="sitegp")) %>% 
  mutate(
    # site order matches the randomization order (must match the constrained space file)
    sitenew = factor(sitenew, levels = site_order),
    # transformed EORTC at each analyzed time point (eortc_6norm, eortc_12norm, ...)
    across(all_of(paste0("eortc_", eortc_months)), eortc_trans, .names = "{.col}norm")) |> 
  set_variable_labels(ecog3 = "ECOG",
                      enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry", 
                      arm_c = "Arm",
                      crpc_per = "Disease state") %>% 
  set_variable_labels(.labels = setNames(
    as.list(paste0("EORTC at ", eortc_months, " mo (transformed)")),
    paste0("eortc_", eortc_months, "norm"))) %>% 
  # add technical bug exposure
  full_join(bug_outcome, by="subject") %>% 
  mutate(bug_group = case_when(
    !is.na(bug_group) ~ bug_group,
    arm=="control" ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ 4),
    bug_group = factor(bug_group, 
                       levels = 0:4,
                       labels = c("Control", 
                                  "No questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "Some intervention questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "All intervention questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "No intervention questionnaires completed")),
    # exposure to the bug: enrolled after the fix, or no questionnaires affected = not impacted
    full_dose = case_when(
      arm=="control" ~ 0,
      empro_cnstdate > bug_fix_date | bug_group=="No questionnaires impacted by bug" ~ 1, 
      TRUE ~ 2),
    full_dose = factor(full_dose, levels = 0:2, labels = c("Control", "Not impacted by bug", "Impacted by bug")))

# complete cases at each time point
analysis_data6  <- analysis_data %>% filter(!is.na(eortc_6)) 
analysis_data12 <- analysis_data %>% filter(!is.na(eortc_12)) 

# variable names for each time point (raw, transformed, death indicator)
o6  <- outcome_spec(6)
o12 <- outcome_spec(12)

# patient counts
n_crpc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="CRPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_mhspc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="mHSPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_intervention <- analysis_data %>% filter(arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
```

# EORTC Distribution
We investigated the distribution of the primary outcome (EORTC QLQ-c30 composite score at 6 months) to determine if a transformation was needed to fulfill the normality assumption in regression models. EORTC is left skewed, and we found that `r trans` was the best transformation for the data.

# Outcome: EORTC at 6 months

## Permutation test

Intervention effect was analyzed using linear mixed models, with statistical inference based on permutation tests applied to model residuals. The permutations tests are complete case analysis.

### Model 1

Only adjusted for subject-level covariates

```{r perm-6-model1}
# Site order in the constrained space file should be (1 = intervention, 0 = control):
#                                             clustername allocation
# 1                   Queensland University of Technology          0
# 2                                        Eastern Health          1
# 3                         St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney          0
# 4                         Macquarie University Hospital          1
# 5                                Cross Cancer Institute          1
# 6                         Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre          0
# 7                The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 8    Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 9              Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 10 University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 11                     Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center          0
# 12               Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center          1
# 13                         Weill Cornell Medical Center          1
# 14                               University of Virginia          0

perm1 <- run_cptest(analysis_data6, o6$norm, covs = subject_covs)
```

`r perm1$pvalue_statement`

### Model 2

Adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

```{r perm-6-model2}
perm2 <- run_cptest(analysis_data6, o6$norm, covs = adj_terms)
```

`r perm2$pvalue_statement`

## F-test

All models are adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

**Interpretation**: To improve modeling, the outcome was transformed as √(100 − EORTC). This transformation reverses the scale: higher EORTC scores (indicating better quality of life) become smaller values, while lower EORTC scores (worse quality of life) become larger values.  

Because of this reversal, the direction of effects in the model is also reversed:

-   Factors with positive coefficients are associated with worse quality of life (lower EORTC)

-   Factors with negative coefficients are associated with better quality of life (higher EORTC) 

Importantly, this does not change the underlying clinical relationships—it only reflects how the outcome was mathematically transformed.

### Complete case analysis

```{r cc-6-model}
# linear mixed model (singular-fit warnings: site random-effect variance can be estimated as ~0)
fit_cc6 <- fit_cc_model(analysis_data6, o6$norm)

tbl_cc_regression(fit_cc6, caption = "**Complete case analysis of primary outcome**")
```


#### Model diagnostics

These plots show normality of the residuals from the mixed model, which further supports the transformation of the outcome, EORTC.

```{r cc-6-diagnostics, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
plot_lmm_diagnostics(fit_cc6)
```

### Missing at random (MAR)

The first imputation analysis assumes that data are missing at random. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with predictive mean matching (`r n_imp` imputations). Linear mixed models with a random intercept for site were fitted within each imputed dataset and pooled using Rubin’s rules. The outcome was analyzed on the transformed scale. Global p‑values for categorical predictors were obtained using ANOVA (F-test). Adjusted marginal means were back‑transformed to the original scale for interpretability.

Model coefficients and confidence intervals were pooled across imputations using Rubin’s rules. Global p‑values for categorical variables with \>2 levels were obtained using ANOVA, which combines information across imputations while accounting for correlations among category levels.

```{r mi-6-mar, results="hide"}
# impute on the transformed scale -> fit the mixed model in each imputation -> global p-values
mar6 <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o6, mi_scenarios$mar)
```

```{r mi-6-mar-table}
tbl_mi_regression(mar6)
```


### Missing not at random (MNAR)

Based on the relationship between ECOG and missingness of EORTC scores, we hypothesize that data are not missing at random. To try to more accurately impute data we use the following steps:

-   Participants who were deceased prior to the 6-month EORTC were assigned an EORTC score of 0.

-   Imputation for missing EORTC scores for participants alive at 6 months was done according to the methods from Carerras ACTION study method: <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-020-01180-y> 

#### Large shifts

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted as follows: `r describe_shifts(delta_large)`. This reflects increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status.

##### Fixed shift (MNAR)

A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The fixed shift was applied to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.

```{r mi-6-fixed_large, results="hide"}
fixed6_large <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o6, mi_scenarios$fixed_large)
```

```{r mi-6-fixed-table_large}
tbl_mi_regression(fixed6_large)
```

##### Variable shift (MNAR)

For participants alive at 6 months with a missing EORTC score, we assumed that a proportion of non-responders had worse unobserved QoL than predicted under MAR. Within each imputed dataset, each such participant was shifted downward on the original EORTC scale by an ECOG-specific amount (`r shift_list(delta_large)`) with probability p (ECOG-specific; `r p_text(mi_scenarios$variable_large$p_shift)`); the remaining participants were imputed under MAR. 

```{r mi-6-variable_large, results="hide"}
variable6_large <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o6, mi_scenarios$variable_large)
```

```{r mi-6-variable-table_large}
tbl_mi_regression(variable6_large)
```

#### More conservative shifts

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted as follows: `r describe_shifts(delta_small)`. This reflects increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status.

##### Fixed shift (MNAR)

A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The fixed shift was applied to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.

```{r mi-6-fixed_small, results="hide"}
fixed6_small <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o6, mi_scenarios$fixed_small)
```

```{r mi-6-fixed-table_small}
tbl_mi_regression(fixed6_small)
```

##### Variable shift (MNAR)

For participants alive at 6 months with a missing EORTC score, we assumed that a proportion of non-responders had worse unobserved QoL than predicted under MAR. Within each imputed dataset, each such participant was shifted downward on the original EORTC scale by an ECOG-specific amount (`r shift_list(delta_small)`) with probability p (ECOG-specific; `r p_text(mi_scenarios$variable_small$p_shift)`); the remaining participants were imputed under MAR. 

```{r mi-6-variable_small, results="hide"}
variable6_small <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o6, mi_scenarios$variable_small)
```

```{r mi-6-variable-table_small}
tbl_mi_regression(variable6_small)
```

### Back-transformed estimates

Estimated marginal means, back-transformed to the original EORTC scale.

```{r}
emm_table_combined(fit_cc6, list(mar6, fixed6_large, fixed6_small, variable6_large, variable6_small),
                   method_labels = c("Complete case", 
                                     "MAR", 
                                     "MNAR - large fixed shift", 
                                     "MNAR - small fixed shift", 
                                     "MNAR - large variable shift",
                                     "MNAR - small variable shift"))
```

### Compare distributions of EORTC

These plots show the distributions of outcomes for the various models, including the complete cases and the data generated for each imputation method. Note that the values are on the transformed scale, so upward shifts in the distribution on the transformed scale correspond to lower values of EORTC on the native scale.

```{r compare-6, echo=FALSE}
cmp6 <- compare_eortc_distributions(analysis_data, o6$norm, list(mar6, fixed6_large, variable6_large))
cmp6$overall   # all participants
cmp6$by_ecog   # stratified by ECOG
```

## Effect of technical bug
The effect of the EMPRO technical bug (thank you module not showing personalized self-management content) is analyzed using complete case analysis with a linear mixed model (F-test). A new exposure variable was created to represent the extent to which the technical bug affected each participant.

#### Bug presence 
```{r bug-presence}
analysis_data %>% 
  select(yn_eortc_6, full_dose) %>% 
  mutate(yn_eortc_6 = factor(yn_eortc_6, levels = c("FALSE", "TRUE"), labels=c("EORTC missing at 6 mo", "EORTC completed at 6 mo"))) %>% 
  set_variable_labels(full_dose = "Bug impact") %>% 
  tbl_summary(by=yn_eortc_6, percent="row") %>% 
  add_overall(last=TRUE) %>% 
  bold_labels() %>% 
  modify_caption("**Summary of participants who started the study after the technical bug was fixed and the number who will drop out of the complete case analysis in each group**")
```

#### Model results

```{r bug-model}
# same complete case model, with bug impact as the exposure instead of arm
fit_bug <- fit_cc_model(analysis_data6, o6$norm, exposure = "full_dose")

tbl_cc_regression(fit_bug,
                  caption = "**Analysis of effect of technical bug on primary outcome - complete case analysis**",
                  global_vars = c("full_dose", global_test_vars))
```

#### Back-transformed estimates

Estimated marginal means, back-transformed to the original EORTC scale.

```{r bug-emm}
emm_table_cc(fit_bug, "full_dose",
             group_label = "Bug Impact",
             title = "Adjusted Mean Composite Scores by Bug Impact",
             subtitle = paste0("Back-transformed estimates from the ", trans, " scale"),
             note = paste("Means were estimated from the mixed model and",
                          "back-transformed to the original composite score scale."))
```

# Outcome: EORTC at 12 months

## Permutation test

Intervention effect was analyzed using linear mixed models, with statistical inference based on permutation tests applied to model residuals. The permutations tests are complete case analysis.

### Model 1

Only adjusted for subject-level covariates

```{r perm-12-model1}
perm1 <- run_cptest(analysis_data12, o12$norm, covs = subject_covs)
```

`r perm1$pvalue_statement`

### Model 2

Adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

```{r perm-12-model2}
perm2 <- run_cptest(analysis_data12, o12$norm, covs = adj_terms)
```

`r perm2$pvalue_statement`

## F-test

All models are adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

**Interpretation**: To improve modeling, the outcome was transformed as √(100 − EORTC). This transformation reverses the scale: higher EORTC scores (indicating better quality of life) become smaller values, while lower EORTC scores (worse quality of life) become larger values.  

Because of this reversal, the direction of effects in the model is also reversed:

-   Factors with positive coefficients are associated with worse quality of life (lower EORTC)

-   Factors with negative coefficients are associated with better quality of life (higher EORTC) 

Importantly, this does not change the underlying clinical relationships—it only reflects how the outcome was mathematically transformed.

### Complete case analysis


```{r cc-12-model}
fit_cc12 <- fit_cc_model(analysis_data12, o12$norm)

tbl_cc_regression(fit_cc12, caption = "**Complete case analysis of primary outcome**")
```

#### Model diagnostics

These plots show normality of the residuals from the mixed model, which further supports the transformation of the outcome, EORTC.

```{r cc-12-diagnostics, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
plot_lmm_diagnostics(fit_cc12)
```

### Missing at random (MAR)

The first imputation analysis assumes that data are missing at random. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with predictive mean matching (`r n_imp` imputations). Linear mixed models with a random intercept for site were fitted within each imputed dataset and pooled using Rubin’s rules. The outcome was analyzed on the transformed scale. Global p‑values for categorical predictors were obtained using ANOVA (F-test). Adjusted marginal means were back‑transformed to the original scale for interpretability.  

Model coefficients and confidence intervals were pooled across imputations using Rubin’s rules. Global p‑values for categorical variables with \>2 levels were obtained using ANOVA, which combines information across imputations while accounting for correlations among category levels.

```{r mi-12-mar, results="hide"}
mar12 <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o12, mi_scenarios$mar)
```

```{r mi-12-mar-table}
tbl_mi_regression(mar12)
```

### Missing not at random (MNAR)


Based on the relationship between ECOG and missingness of EORTC scores, we hypothesize that data are not missing at random. To try to more accurately impute data we use the following steps:

-   Participants who were deceased prior to the 12-month EORTC were assigned an EORTC score of 0.

-   Imputation for missing EORTC scores for participants alive at 12 months was done according to the methods from Carerras ACTION study method: <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-020-01180-y> 

#### Large shifts

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted as follows: `r describe_shifts(delta_large)`. This reflects increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status.

##### Fixed shift (MNAR)

A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The fixed shift was applied to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.

```{r mi-12-fixed_large, results="hide"}
fixed12_large <- run_mi_scenario(analysis_data, o12, mi_scenarios$fixed_large)
```

```{r mi-12-fixed-table_large}
tbl_mi_regression(fixed12_large)
```

##### Variable shift (MNAR)

For participants alive at 12 months with a missing EORTC score, we assumed that a proportion of non-responders had worse unobserved QoL than predicted under MAR. Within each imputed dataset, each such participant was shifted downward on the original EORTC scale by an ECOG-specific amount (`r shift_list(delta_large)`) with probability p (ECOG-specific; `r p_text(mi_scenarios$variable_large$p_shift)`); the remaining participants were imputed under MAR. 

```{r mi-12-variable_large, results="hide"}

```

```{r mi-12-variable-table_large}

```

#### More conservative shifts

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted as follows: `r describe_shifts(delta_small)`. This reflects increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status.

A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The fixed shift was applied to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.

# Overall survival
Participants were censored at the date of their last IRONMAN visit
```{r survival, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7, echo=FALSE}
survfit2(Surv(limbo, dead=="Yes") ~ arm_c, data = analysis_data) %>% 
  ggsurvfit(linewidth=2) +
  add_censor_mark(size = 2) +
  add_risktable(risktable_stats = c("{n.risk}"),
                size = 5,
                theme =   
                  list(
                    theme_risktable_default(axis.text.y.size = 14, 
                                            plot.title.size = 14),
                    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
                  )) +
  scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = seq(0, 12, 3))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 12.2)) +
  # update figure labels/titles
  labs(
    y = "Overall Survival",
    x = "Months from EMPRO enrollment",
    title = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r secondary-outcomes, echo=FALSE}
  select(hosp_6mo, hosp_12mo, dead12, censored, arm_c) %>%

  tbl_summary(by = arm_c,

              type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
```
